market_summary: Markets remain split between AI-driven optimism and mounting competitive/regulatory risk. Nvidia's Sept 28 Open Agent Safety Platform launch is a positive but is being offset by fresh (Sept 30) news that DeepSeek is partnering with Huawei to build CUDA alternatives for Ascend chips, a direct long-term threat to Nvidia's software moat. Apple's iPhone 18 Pro is showing strong China demand (12% YoY, 33% share) even as a UK marketplace class-action against Apple/Amazon adds legal overhang. In Singapore, banks have run hard on rate-hike optimism (STI +24.6% YTD) and now look stretched — DBS/OCBC/UOB are all red today after extended multi-month gains — while REITs and industrials with heavy analyst buy ratings (Keppel, CICT) look comparatively less extended.

picks.thesis: Keppel has pulled back modestly (-2.5% 1m, -1.7% today) despite a heavily bullish analyst base (12 buy/1 hold/2 sell) and 13.9% implied upside to consensus target. No negative catalyst has emerged; the dip looks like broader SGX profit-taking rather than a company-specific issue, offering a re-entry point.
picks.news: No company-specific news in the past 10 days; SG financials/industrials have been supported by the broader rate-hike rally narrative (background, SGX/STI item, Sept 29).
picks.risks: If the SGX-wide pullback (also seen in DBS/OCBC/UOB/SGX today) is the start of a deeper index correction, Keppel with its higher beta (1.13) and volatility (24.2%) could fall further before recovering.

picks.thesis: CICT shows the most bullish analyst skew on the watchlist (13 buy/3 hold/0 sell, 20.3% implied upside) and elevated relative volume (2.1x 20-day average) suggests accumulation even as price sits 12% below its 52w high and below both MAs. This combination of heavy buy consensus plus unusual volume on a laggard REIT is a reasonable contrarian long.
picks.news: No direct news catalyst found; this call rests on the analyst consensus and volume signal in the price data rather than a headline.
picks.risks: Singapore REITs are rate-sensitive; if the rate-hike narrative driving bank strength persists, higher-for-longer rates could keep pressuring REIT valuations regardless of analyst targets.

picks.thesis: Apple sold off -2.7% today despite genuinely strong iPhone 18 Pro China launch data (12% YoY unit growth, 33% share) reported the same day — the drop looks driven by the UK class-action headline (Sept 28) rather than fundamentals. The China sales strength is the more durable, revenue-relevant data point for the next few quarters.
picks.news: iPhone 18 Pro China launch-week sales +12% YoY, 33% share (Yahoo Finance, Sept 30); UK Competition Appeal Tribunal allowed a £289-306m class action against Apple/Amazon to proceed (Yahoo Finance, Sept 28).
picks.risks: Consensus analyst target is essentially flat to current price (-0.4% implied), so this is a tactical bounce trade, not a re-rating call; further negative legal/regulatory headlines could keep sentiment weak.

picks.thesis: Meta has the strongest price momentum on the watchlist (+27.8% 1m, +3.2% today, vs MA50 +19.4%) with a large buy-heavy analyst base (54 buy/7 hold/1 sell) and 7.5% remaining upside to target even after the run. This is a momentum continuation trade in the absence of contrary news.
picks.news: No specific Meta headline surfaced in this news cycle; the move appears to be part of the broader AI-stock volatility described in the market summary rather than a discrete catalyst.
picks.risks: With no fresh news backing the rally and volatility at 41.8%, a sharp reversal is plausible if AI-sector sentiment turns (as it partly has for Nvidia on the DeepSeek/Huawei news); this is a lower-conviction, news-thin call.

picks.thesis: OCBC is up 94.6% over the past year and 30.5% above its 200-day average, among the most extended of the SGX banks, yet its consensus analyst target (S$31.53) sits slightly below the current price (S$31.99), implying -1.4% expected return. Combined with today's -0.5% decline and a broader SG bank pullback, this looks like the most stretched name to fade within the rate-hike rally.
picks.news: STI hit a record high in early September on bank-rally strength tied to September rate-hike prospects (Straits Times, Sept 29, background); no new positive catalyst since.
picks.risks: If the SG rate-hike/bank-rally narrative continues and OCBC's upcoming results beat expectations, the stock could keep grinding higher regardless of the stretched technical picture.

picks.thesis: Today's news that DeepSeek is partnering with Huawei to build TileLang, a CUDA alternative for Ascend chips, is a fresh and structurally important threat to Nvidia's software moat in China, even as the positive Open Agent Safety Platform launch (Sept 28) gets more headline attention. The stock is only down 0.7% today, suggesting the market has not yet fully digested the competitive risk, which could weigh over coming weeks even as Nvidia's near-term US demand story stays intact.
picks.news: DeepSeek partners with Huawei on chip programming tools (TileLang) to reduce reliance on Nvidia, reported Sept 30, Straits Times; Nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform launched with 100+ partners, Sept 28, Yahoo Finance.
picks.risks: Nvidia's near-term revenue is overwhelmingly non-China and driven by hyperscaler AI capex, so this China-specific software threat may take years to materially dent earnings; consensus analyst target implies 44% upside, and any strong earnings beat would overwhelm this thesis quickly.
